Stakeholder / investor-relations note · Maps to E8 (Stakeholder & Investor Relations — the analyst Q&A as accountability), Course 04 (Competitive Strategy — who holds power over JPM), Course 05 (Marketing — partner quotes as proof), E4 (Governance — proxy advisors, regulators) · Written 2026-10-25 · Companion to jpmc people and tradeweb outside voices

  • Source: _ingest/raw/jpmc/articles.jsonl: analyst questions on ten earnings calls and at the 2025 Investor Day; partner, client and expert quotes in 140 web items (Kinexys releases, Markets articles, research pages); and outside parties Dimon argues with in the letters. JPM mentions in the Tradeweb corpus are marked [TW]. No independent press was collected. Every outside voice here was chosen by JPMC, except the analysts, who chose their own questions.
  • Core claim: Four groups speak about JPMC in its own corpus. (1) Sell-side analysts are the only consistent skeptics. Mike Mayo (Wells Fargo) asked questions on every one of the ten calls read, mostly on expense and technology returns, and on succession. Others pressed on capital return, stablecoins, private credit, agentic AI and the co-president choice. (2) Partners and clients (Coinbase, Mastercard, Siemens, BMW, B2C2, Ethereum Institutional, BlackRock) praise the rails, not JPM's economics. (3) Experts quoted on JPM pages supply the strongest counterarguments to JPM's own theses: depegs (Better Markets), deposit-token reach (Fireblocks), agentic-AI risk (SEDA), the "invisible bubble" in volatility (Prescient), and Risk magazine on "run-the-bank" vs "change-the-bank". (4) Regulators, proxy advisors and aggregators appear only as Dimon's opponents. Power over JPM sits with regulators first, the largest institutional clients second and nonbank competitors third. Venues hold little visible power in this corpus, which itself is a JPM position (jpmc markets venues).

2. The analysts: what they challenged and what they got

Call Analyst Challenge (verbatim where quoted) Answer
4Q20 (2021-01-15) Mayo "spending is certain. Returns are uncertain." PayPal, Stripe, Visa and Mastercard "trounce the valuation of your stock, so I think the market's saying that others are going to win." Dimon: "Mike, we never said we missed it."
4Q20 Chubak Waiting for G-SIB recalibration ("Waiting for Godot") Dimon: "Probably not in our lifetimes."
4Q21 (2022-01-14) Mayo "It's a little frustrating, this call, because the guidance you've given has given all the bad news without any targets." Also: "you're spending the rate hikes for investments over the next 10 years." Dimon: "I feel your pain and your frustration". No targets given
4Q21 Mitchell, Graseck, Schorr Payback on doubled investment spend Barnum: returns "impossible to prove" in a narrow sense
4Q22 (2023-01-13) Mayo "this is the third year in a row of about $5 billion of expense growth." Accountability for the "Frank" deal Dimon: "a huge mistake"
4Q23 (2024-01-12) Mayo Tech budget and AI share of the $90B expense guide Barnum defers to Investor Day
4Q24 (2025-01-15) Mayo "who's your successor?" "four, five years or more" (jpmc succession)
Investor Day 2025 Alexopoulos "Iron Man never retired." "four more years and maybe two more"
Investor Day 2025 Schorr Is ~$13B of direct lending small versus a $1–2T market? Rohrbaugh: origination, not assets
4Q25 (2026-01-13) Mayo Breakdown of the ~$9B expense increase and AI payoff Dimon: "part of you has to trust me, I'm sorry"
4Q25 Schorr Stablecoin interest and a Treasury estimate of $6.6T of deposits at risk Barnum: "parallel ecosystem" risk
2Q26 (2026-07-14) Martinez Are AI benefits underestimated, given Block's 40% workforce cut? Dimon: "30% or 40%" cuts in discrete areas
2Q26 Mayo "we have a FX trader now selling mortgage, credit cards and deposits" Dimon defends cross-firm experience
2Q26 Najarian, Usdin Succession timing and traits "Several years... plus or minus"
3Q26 (2026-10-13) Mayo AI spend (~$2B?) versus benefits Barnum: ~$700M; benefits "aren't observable"
3Q26 Poonawala Agentic AI and "rogue agents" Dimon: no outside agents inside the bank
3Q26 Najarian Buyback cut to ~$1B Organic deployment, the SRI
3Q26 Cassidy IMF warning on hedge funds Dimon: "We worry about a lot of stuff, not what the IMF thinks about it."

Pattern: analysts ask for targets and returns. Management gives doctrine ("output, not an input", "table stakes", "trust me"). Over six years the only quantitative concession was Barnum cutting the AI-spend figure down in 3Q26.

Self-interest flags on JPM's own op-eds: - Melissa Feldsher on open banking: "It is a government-protected subsidy for data middlemen." JPM earns fees from aggregators. - Rachid Alaoui on EU equities defends systematic internalisers, which JPM runs. - Farooq and Muriungi argue against stablecoin "rewards", which protects the deposit-token asymmetry (jpmc kinexys deposit tokens).

4. What the Tradeweb corpus adds [TW]

  • Risk.net (2019): Tradeweb had "long been viewed – and sometimes maligned – as a hostage to the interests of big dealers". JPM was one of those dealers (tradeweb outside voices).
  • Business Insider (2019): JPM's Koo on portfolio trading: "we expect this to double in the next couple of years, if not triple".
  • FT (Feb 2021): "JPMorgan recently surveyed its asset management clients, and they predicted that 40 per cent of all their corporate bond trading will be electronic by 2022."
  • JPMAM as client: McClinchie: "I just started releasing all of my orders from my OMS to Tradeweb".

5. Who holds power over JPM (inference)

  1. Regulators. They set capital, the binding constraint on Markets and on returns. Every letter spends its longest section on them.
  2. The largest institutional clients. Wallet consolidation (client share up 230bp since 2019) makes the top asset managers and hedge funds both JPM's best customers and its biggest negotiators. BlackRock shows up as client, counterparty and voice.
  3. Nonbank competitors. Citadel Securities in markets, Stripe and Block in payments, and stablecoin issuers in deposits set the price ceilings. Dimon names them.
  4. Analysts and investors. They can't force targets, but six years of Mayo's questions forced the 3Q26 AI-spend correction.
  5. Venues. They have little visible power in JPM's own telling, but real power where the dealer needs distribution (Treasury algos, credit). The ICE–MarketAxess and Tradeweb–Trumid consolidation could raise it (ice hub, marketaxess hub).

6. Canon lenses

  • Influence and social proof (canon cialdini influence): partner quotes in Kinexys releases (Coinbase, Mastercard, Ethereum) are social proof for a contested product.
  • Co-opetition (canon brandenburger nalebuff coopetition): Coinbase is client, partner (consumer link) and rival (Base stablecoin flows) at once.
  • Agency and accountability (canon jensen meckling agency theory): the analyst Q&A is the only live accountability channel in the corpus. Its weakness is that management can decline to answer.

Role-play: you are Mike Mayo before the 4Q26 call (Jan 2027). Using only this note and the linked notes, write five one-line questions, one each on expense, AI return, capital, succession and Kinexys. Each must cite a specific number JPM has given. Then predict the one-sentence answer each would get, based on the pattern in §2.
